minors.issue: ParseRecipient wraps age.ParseX25519Recipient's error, which quotes the whole input. When the input is an identity, the error holds the secret key. ParseIdentity uses a fixed error for this reason; ParseRecipient does not.
minors.scenario: A later caller (for example a W3-2 --recipient flag) is handed AGE-SECRET-KEY-1… by mistake. ParseRecipient fails with `not an age X25519 recipient (age1…): malformed recipient "AGE-SECRET-KEY-1…": …` and the CLI prints the secret to stderr. No path in this ticket passes secret text here, so nothing leaks today.

minors.issue: age-deps denies filippo.io/age only in the packages it lists. ADR-0015 decision 2 says it is denied everywhere except internal/keys. tools/pipeline is in the main module and is not covered, and neither is any package added later. main.allow now permits age.
minors.scenario: A file under tools/pipeline/ or a new internal/auth package imports filippo.io/age, and `make lint` passes. huma-deps uses `$all` plus `!**/internal/api/**`, which covers new packages.

minors.issue: The comment says depguard file exclusions do not work, so it lists every package. huma-deps, a few lines above, relies on exactly such an exclusion, so the comment gives a false reason for the narrower rule.
minors.scenario: A maintainer trusts the comment and copies the per-package list for the next restricted module. That rule also misses new packages.
